subject: Pillar Health - urgent AZ2 throughput spike & cross-region evacuation
content:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@pillarhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike - us-west2 (AZ2) - immediate help needed

Hi Karthik / Monica,

We’re seeing a severe degradation out of our us-west2 AZ2 serving tier starting ~08:45 PDT. Customers are hitting 5xx error rates up to 8% and p95 latency has jumped from ~220ms to >3.2s for generation endpoints. Throughput for our key policy route has dropped by ~45%. This is impacting billing and realtime workflows.

We’ve attached a snapshot of the error distribution and a short log extract. Can Redwood route traffic away from AZ2 to maintain SLA while you investigate? We need a short-term mitigation and ETA on fix.

Attachments: pill_health_error_snapshot_0410.png (PNG, 420KB)

—
Emily Chen
Head of Platform Ops, Pillar Health
emily.chen@pillarhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

-----
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:23:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike - us-west2 (AZ2) - immediate help needed

Thanks Emily — putting this on emergency. I’ve kicked off targeted metric pulls and asked infra on-call to gather kernel/driver traces from the GPU nodes in us-west2 AZ2.

Immediate ask for us (to Pillar): can you share a small sample request-id we can use to trace through our logs? Also, do you have a preference for cross-region traffic — us-west1 or us-east1?

I’ll loop in Rishi and Lauri (ops lead) for exec-level visibility. We’ll follow up in 15.

—
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:37:48 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Pillar Health us-west2 AZ2 throughput collapse — propose split/evacuate plan

Team —

Summary of what we’ve confirmed so far:
- Error rates peaked at 8.1% between 08:43–08:57 PDT; p95 latency for generation routes rose to 3.2–3.5s.
- Autoscaler shows node churn in AZ2 (two machines that had degraded NVLink health) but control plane still sees capacity reported as up.
- Customer requests we steer traffic to avoid impacting their realtime pipelines.

Proposed immediate mitigation (temporary, non-disruptive):
1) Activate per-account circuit breaker for Pillar to cap concurrent inflight to 60% of target to reduce tail queuing (apply on request ingress).
2) Configure routing policy: route new requests from Pillar in us-west2->us-west1 fallback with gradual ramp (10% steps every 2 minutes) until 90% traffic moved or metrics stabilize.
3) Keep read/write KV caches active to avoid cold-start regressions.
4) Stand up an isolated dedicated canary in us-west1 with WarmWarm pool to ensure KV sync.

Requesting permission to proceed from Rishi/Laura for cross-region ramp and exec notification to Pillar (they asked for the routing). We’ll coordinate with infra to mark suspected hosts and gather disk/kernel traces.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:05:13 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Pillar Health us-west2 AZ2 throughput collapse — propose split/evacuate plan

Thanks Karthik — good clear plan. Authorize the cross-region ramp to us-west1. Two operational constraints:
- Do not exceed Pillar’s SLA routing cap for regional failover (we have explicit per-account policy: max 95% redirected without exec approval).
- Keep an automatic fallback: if p95 > 1s or 5xx > 1% in target region, immediately revert and throttle.

Action items assigned:
- Karthik + Aditya: execute routing ramp (start 10% -> 90% as proposed). Tag the runbook steps and update the HubSpot incident record with timestamps.
- Monica: stay on the bridge with Pillar and collate request IDs and logs.
- Laura: coordinate infra for host isolation and collect driver traces; confirm whether NVLink errors match known kernel bug.

I’m escalating to the Exec Operations channel and copying CTO on notice. Keep me posted every 15 mins until stable.

—
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:23:19 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Pillar Health us-west2 AZ2 throughput collapse — propose split/evacuate plan

Executing ramp now. First 10% on new route pushed at 10:24 PDT (us-west1 warm pool). Observability: 5xx dropped from 8.1% to 4.2% at 10:27; p95 improved to ~1.1s. Going to 30% now.

Notes: we enabled per-account circuit breaker and left cache affinity enabled per Karthik’s request. Infra reports two nodes with degraded NVLink; isolating and removing from pool. Laura — please confirm driver logs when you have them.

—
Aditya Rao
SRE, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@pillarhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Pillar Health us-west2 AZ2 throughput collapse — propose split/evacuate plan

Team —

Thanks — traffic ramp and circuit breaker worked. Our pipelines recovered; error rates are back under 0.5% and latency p95 is ~210ms on the routed region. We’ll keep monitoring but you can close the incident when infra confirms host remediation.

We also appreciate the proactive exec loop — product leadership was watching and this was handled smoothly. Please send a short incident summary that we can file on our side.

Attachments: incident_playbook_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Best,
Emily
Head of Platform Ops, Pillar Health
